subject.title: fix(msteams): add timeouts to file consent upload requests

question: Should Microsoft Teams uploads adopt the proposed five-minute base plus 256 KiB/s size budget, with this narrower consent-upload PR landing before the overlapping SharePoint-send PR?
rationale: The code and proof establish correct abort behavior, but source inspection cannot determine whether this production throughput floor is acceptable for supported tenants or which overlapping branch should own the shared helper.

options.title: Approve and land consent first
options.body: Approve the shared timeout formula, resolve this branch's main conflict, land the narrower consent path, then rebase https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/104288 onto the canonical helper.

options.title: Land SharePoint work first
options.body: Make https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/104288 the shared-helper owner, then rebase this PR to add only the file-consent call site and its focused tests.

options.title: Revise the transfer policy
options.body: Pause both PRs until a Microsoft Teams owner selects a more conservative throughput floor or another bounded policy backed by tenant evidence.

recommendation.title: Approve and land consent first
recommendation.body: Approve the shared timeout formula, resolve this branch's main conflict, land the narrower consent path, then rebase https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/104288 onto the canonical helper.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the publicly identified Microsoft Teams maintainer and merged the two changes that established the current consent-upload path.
